question.value: Is there a dusty exo-Kuiper (cometary) belt around TRAPPIST-1, and what initial planetesimal belt masses are allowed by the non-detection after collisional evolution?

evidence.quote: Here we present new and deep ALMA observations of TRAPPIST-1 to look for an exo-Kuiper belt which can provide clues about the formation and architecture of this system.
We observed TRAPPIST-1 using ALMA band 7 (0.88 mm) as part of the project 2017.1.00215.S (PI: S. Marino).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.00215.S and ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.A.00013.S.

claims.hypothesis: Does TRAPPIST-1 host detectable cold dust from an exo-Kuiper belt?
claims.experiment: Deep ALMA band 7 continuum imaging with tclean and aperture flux limits
claims.result: No dust emission; 3 sigma limit 23 uJy for a compact belt and 150 uJy for a 100 au belt
claims.finding: Fractional luminosity above ~2e-5 at 10-100 au is excluded

evidence.quote: Our observations at 0.88 mm did not detect dust emission

claims.hypothesis: What initial planetesimal belts are allowed by the non-detection after ~8 Gyr?
claims.experiment: Compare collisional cascade model predictions with the 3 sigma surface density limit
claims.result: Model dust beyond 40 au would be detectable for a MMSN belt; interior to 40 au the prediction is below the limit
claims.finding: A MMSN-like belt (>~20 Earth masses) beyond 40 au is ruled out, while interior to 40 au collisional evolution alone explains the non-detection

evidence.quote: Beyond 40 au, our model predicts dust levels that would be detectable.
hence collisional evolution alone can explain our disc non-detection

claims.hypothesis: Was most of the available solid mass used to form the known planets?
claims.experiment: Compare the solid mass upper limit with the mass in TRAPPIST-1 planets
claims.result: The upper limit is comparable to the planets' mass
claims.finding: It is possible that most of the solid mass was transported inwards and used to form the planets

evidence.quote: thus it possible that most of the available solid mass in these systems was transported inwards and used to form the known planets.

claims.hypothesis: Is the putative outer belt of Proxima Cen consistent with collisional evolution?
claims.experiment: Apply the same model to re-imaged archival ACA and 12m ALMA data
claims.result: ACA data could have marginally detected a 10-40 au belt as massive as a MMSN; discs below a tenth of a MMSN fall below the limit
claims.finding: The outer belt is consistent with a belt born with a tenth of a MMSN

evidence.quote: This means that the marginal detection of an outer belt at 30 au by (cite: Anglada2017) is consistent with our collisional evolution model and a belt that was born with a tenth of a MMSN.

claims.hypothesis: Is there variable (flare) emission from TRAPPIST-1 at 0.88 mm?
claims.experiment: Image visibilities in 12 s time bins and measure the flux at the stellar position
claims.result: No significant variable emission above the noise; three single 3 sigma peaks in 1400 points
claims.finding: No flares detected, with a 5 sigma limit of 1.2 mJy over 12 s

evidence.quote: We do not find any significant variable emission above the noise level

referee_caveats_inferred: Upper limits depend on adopted dust opacity (3 cm2/g), temperature law and belt width fraction (0.5), whose uncertainty is not propagated
Collisional model is not released or fully specified, so conclusions about belts beyond 40 au cannot be independently reproduced
Age of 7.6+-2.2 Gyr is drawn from the literature and dominates the collisional depletion conclusion
Proxima Cen limits rely on an azimuthally averaged, assumed 45 deg inclination disc with few imaging details given

missing_for_reproduction: CASA/pipeline versions, tclean parameters and beam size
Collisional evolution model code and input files
Proxima Cen project/imaging details and the CO non-LTE inputs
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Tens of GB of raw/calibrated visibilities for 6 TRAPPIST-1 execution blocks (4.5 h on source), plus Proxima Cen 12m and ACA data of unknown size
reproducibility.score_reason: Observation setup and headline numbers are given, but imaging parameters, CASA version, the upper-limit procedure and the unreleased collisional model are missing, and public availability is not stated.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The paper does not state that the data are public, and the collisional-evolution part of the recipe cannot be redone from the text; only the continuum upper limits could be approximated.
